findings.notes: CEL policy expressions were compiled without a cost limit, so the work one expression could do was unbounded and a policy author could exhaust a shared controller. Enabling cel-go's cost limit alone does not help, because cel-go prices O(n) operations by resolved overload ID and Kyverno declares its resource variables as dyn, so every such call is billed a flat 1 unit; fixed by pricing calls by function name, refusing operations whose predicted output exceeds a size cap before they run, and metering the total cost of one request, all delivered as environment-level program options so every policy family and the legacy kyverno.io/v1 CEL path inherit them (PR #1028).
